thread_text:
maria_support: Hey team, customer Acme (tenant acme-123) just reported their monthly token balance dropped to 0 at 2026-03-08T14:02:11Z. Their billing window should reset 2026-03-09T08:00:00-08:00 (America/Los_Angeles). They claim no extra usage. Can we triage?

jamal_sre: Can you paste the tenant id + a sample request/response headers (from one of their calls) showing x-credits-remaining / x-reset-at if available? Also what UI time did they see zero?

maria_support: Copied from customer screenshot and logs:

Customer UI timestamp: 2026-03-08 06:02 PST (shows 0)
Sample request (redacted):

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-***" -H "X-Tenant: acme-123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Response headers: 
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-credits-remaining: 0
x-credits-reset-at: 2026-03-09T16:00:00Z
x-rate-limit-remaining: 498

They say backend returned 200 but header shows 0. They expected reset at 2026-03-09T16:00:00Z (which is 00:00 PT on 3/9) so that reset_at matches. But UI shows zero 18 hours before the reset time.

alex_engineer: Two quick checks: 1) whether the refill cron job ran on our side (monthly_rollover job), 2) whether our admin cache/edge was serving stale zero state.

jamal_sre: I pulled the job logs. monthly_rollover for tenant acme-123 last ran: 2026-02-09T08:00:12-08:00 (expected). Next scheduled run: 2026-03-09T08:00:01-08:00. No run recorded on 2026-03-08. There was a transient DB failover during 2026-03-08 05:58-06:05 PST window per infra alerts (K8s node flapping). Could be related.

tess_ce: Customer says they were on a long-running streaming session that started 2026-03-07 and had infrequent heartbeats. Could that keep an old header value cached at the edge or in the UI?

jamal_sre: Yes, streaming can keep connections open and our edge caching layer can serve a cached quota header for long polls. But x-credits-remaining is generated at the token-issuer service at request time and should be fresh. We need to verify where 0 originated.

alex_engineer: Running quick repro against production sandbox for acme-123:

# check DB quota record
SELECT tenant_id, credits_remaining, reset_at, updated_at FROM tenant_quotas WHERE tenant_id = 'acme-123' ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1;
-- returned credits_remaining: 0, reset_at: 2026-03-09T16:00:00Z, updated_at: 2026-03-08T05:59:58Z

This matches the header time. Something wrote 0 into the DB at ~05:59:58 PST.

maria_support: Any write logs around that time? Who/what wrote it?

jamal_sre: Trace found: monthly_rollover_runner attempted to create a new monthly bucket in a transaction, but at 2026-03-08T05:59:58Z there was a retry from the refill-worker due to a timeout on a previous attempt at 05:59:56Z. The refill-worker has an edge case where on retry path it sets credits_remaining = coalesce(existing,0) + delta; if existing is read as null due to transient DB read error, it falls back to 0 before adding delta, but the code path for delta failed to commit due to the timeout, leaving the 0 write. This is a bug.

alex_engineer: Repro steps I used locally:
1) Simulate DB read returning null for tenant_quotas.getCurrent()
2) Run refill-worker retry path
3) Observe intermediate write credits_remaining=0 committed before the increment transaction completes.

Code snippet of vulnerable block:
```
current = tenant_quotas.getCurrent(tenant)
if not current:
    current = {"credits_remaining": 0}
# retry path
tenant_quotas.upsert(tenant, current)
# later increment happens in a separate step and can fail
```

jamal_sre: TL;DR: race between DB failover and our retry logic caused an early write of zero. That explains the customer's header and DB state. Because reset_at is still in the future, UI shows 0 but the scheduled reset still targets the right time.

tess_ce: What's the mitigation? Customer is stuck with 0 until the scheduled reset in ~18 hours. Can we do an emergency refill? They are on a paid Dedicated plan.

maria_support: Customer requests immediate fix. They're production-critical.

jamal_sre: We have an admin API to apply an ad-hoc credit grant. I'll do a manual refill and follow with a permanent patch. Manual command:

curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer admin-***" -H "Content-Type: application/json" https://admin.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/acme-123/refill -d '{"credits": 200000}'

(Executed at 2026-03-08T07:03:21Z) -> admin response 200 OK. Verified DB: credits_remaining = 200000, updated_at 2026-03-08T07:03:22Z. I also invalidated edge cache for tenant headers.

maria_support: Customer confirms UI now shows tokens and resumed streaming. :tada:

alex_engineer: I'll open a PR with the safe-refill patch: ensure we compute increment in-memory first and then write a single upsert atomic operation, and add guard against treating null as permanent zero. Will add feature test covering DB failover path.

jamal_sre: Also created incident INC-2026-0456 and linked a follow-up ticket SRE-372 for the code fix + add extra observability (emit "refill-retry-fallback" metric).

maria_support: Noted. I'll reply to customer with root-cause summary + the incident number and confirm the top-up we applied and the follow-up timeline.

billingbot: Automated note: manual refill of 200000 tokens applied to tenant acme-123 by jamal_sre at 2026-03-08T07:03:21Z. Billing impact: pro-rated charge pending approval (invoice hold created).

maria_support: Thanks everyone. Closing thread after customer ack and patch merged.
